steps.name: Differential expression: DESeq2 Wald + apeglm, edgeR QL robustness
caveats: Length offset: the record does not state whether the Salmon gene-level table was length-corrected, and no per-sample quantification files or average transcript length table are provided — fit the count model on the counts as delivered with no length offset; do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input. State in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression.
With 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets the gene's p-values to NA; keep this behavior on and report the flagged genes.
Do not select genes by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone.
Determine the condition levels from metadata.csv and set the reference level explicitly — never rely on alphabetical level ordering.
steps.context: Inputs: counts.csv (12,000 x 12, Salmon gene-level counts as delivered — no length correction stated, no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table) and metadata.csv (sample, condition; read the actual condition levels from the file, expected aldosterone vs vehicle). Design: 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch. Downstream consumer: T2S2.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed in the aldosterone-treated samples compared with the vehicle controls, and which transcription factor genes are among them?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca; edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method for report robustness per R-0042@54e1; counts as delivered without length offset per R-0169@18ab.

constraints: robustness: second method = edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and same design; report significant counts per method and the intersection size
steps.description: Minimal pre-filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size (6) of samples. Build the DESeqDataSet on the counts as delivered with no length offset (see caveats), design ~ condition with the reference level explicitly set to the control level (vehicle) and the contrast named as factor/aldosterone/vehicle so that a positive log2 fold change means higher expression in the treated samples. Wald test, apeglm log fold change shrinkage, independent filtering on, Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment at alpha 0.05, and a p-value histogram inspected before trusting the adjusted values. As the robustness second method, run the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design, and report the number of significant genes per method and the size of their intersection (the intersection is the high-confidence set). Export for the TF-activity step: the pre-filtered count matrix, the log2 CPM (normalized) matrix for all 12 samples, the full results table (baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken LFC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj), and the DE gene list (padj < 0.05).
acceptance_criteria: Results table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken LFC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj; genes selected by padj < 0.05 only
Number of genes with NA p-values from the count-outlier flag reported separately from the genes dropped by the independent filter
Unadjusted p-value histogram saved and its shape described
edgeR QL results and the two-method overlap count reported
Exported: pre-filtered count matrix, log2 CPM matrix (12 samples), DE gene list (padj < 0.05), both methods' results tables

plan.title: Aldosterone-treated vs vehicle kidney: TF drivers
plan.analytical_narrative: Question: which transcription factors drive the response of the 6 aldosterone-treated kidney samples compared with the 6 vehicle controls. Flow: (1) T1S1 sample-structure QC — blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap on the 12,000 x 12 Salmon gene-level counts verify that the samples separate 6 vs 6 by condition before any test; metadata has no batch column (single batch), so plots are colored by condition only. (2) T1S2 defines the response: DESeq2 on the counts as delivered — the profile does not state whether the Salmon gene table was length-corrected, and no per-sample quant files or average transcript length table accompany it, so no length offset is applied and that limitation is carried into the report; median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), explicit reference level vehicle, contrast aldosterone/vehicle (positive LFC = higher in treated), Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected; the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design is the second method for report robustness. This step also exports the pre-filtered count matrix, the log2 CPM matrix, and the DE gene list (padj < 0.05) that the TF step consumes. (3) T2S2 answers the question directly: VIPER and ARACNe are absent from the environment and 12 samples cannot support an expression-inferred network, so per-sample TF activity is inferred with the decoupleR univariate linear model (ulm) on the per-sample log2 CPM matrix, with the signed CollecTRI human v2.0 prior-knowledge regulons (only regulators with >=5 tested targets), contrasted treated vs control with limma on the score matrix and Benjamini-Hochberg across regulators; the DoRothEA human regulons at confidence A-C run as the alternative network and the overlap/disagreement of top regulators is reported; a JASPAR 2020 promoter motif scan on the DE promoters (background = the other tested genes, sequences from the GRCh38.p13 reference) adds sequence-level support beside the regulon inference. (4) T1S3 consolidates a ranked TF driver list annotated with each TF's own expression status, plus the DE diagnostics and a full reproducibility record. The dataset is small (12k genes x 12 samples), so all steps are light on CPU and memory.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
